author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: A softer October payrolls print and a Fed hold turned the October bond rout into a bull-steepening relief rally (10Y down 21 bps over five observations, VIX down 24.61% over 5 sessions), but the curve is still inverted at -26 bps while growth evidence softens in the US (ISM 46.7%), the euro zone (Q3 GDP -0.1%) and China (October factory contraction). Own quality duration (software, semiconductors, utilities, investment-grade credit) rather than cyclicals, stay underweight China beta, and keep Poland as the high-conviction post-election overweight with the 2024 budget hole as the key risk.
sources_policy: Facts come only from the 2023-11-07 frozen feed (tools/digest.py) and the 2023-11-07 market card (tools/showcard.py); every concrete fact is cited in the same paragraph; numbers come from the card or the cited headline titles; no spot-FX levels or returns are quoted; previews are used only for pending events; company news <=7 days, company results <=14 days, macro/policy baselines <=35 days before the 2023-11-07 00:00 UTC cutoff.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0076 (Guardian, RBA hikes cash rate to 4.35%): the RBA decision was announced on 2023-11-07 after the cutoff; the 2023-11-06 timestamp is misdated. Not cited; RBA treated only as a pending Melbourne Cup Day decision via preview headlines.
n1870 (Reuters, Tesla to build 25,000-euro car in Germany): story appears to have been published on 2023-11-07; timing doubtful, not cited.
n0899 (Guardian, Klarna first quarterly profit in four years): publication timing relative to cutoff uncertain; not cited.

n1516 (Reuters, UK consumer spending slowest in over a year: Barclays): Barclays card-spending data are normally embargoed to 00:01 UK time on the Tuesday, i.e. 2023-11-07 after the cutoff; timestamp looks misdated; not cited (UK manufacturing PMI n1368 used instead).
n0848 (MarketWatch, Taylor Swift is Time's person of the year): refers to a December 2023 event; misdated, not cited.

n0547 (CNBC, best Bank of America credit cards of November 2026), n0122 (Black Friday deals 2026), n1937 (ADP Payroll Review 2026), n0935 (Mercedes-Benz GLC Review 2026): later-dated evergreen pages; not cited.
n1947 (Kevin Drum, core PCE 'spiked to 3.6%'): blog framing of the September PCE print is ambiguous (annualised vs year-on-year); not cited.
n1493, n1499, n1587, n1719, n2052: titles contain numeric spot-FX levels or returns; cited only for direction (n1493, n2052) without quoting any FX number.
October RPP decision size and the BOJ's 2023-10-31 decision are not stated by any eligible headline; omitted. KOSPI's +5.66% session is reported without a cause.
